title: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

topics.title: Need for classification and genesis of periodic classification

concepts.learning_objective: Describe Dobereiner's triads and Newlands' law of octaves and state their limitations.
Explain Mendeleev's periodic law, his placement of elements and his predictions of undiscovered elements.

topics.title: Modern periodic law and the present form of the Periodic Table

concepts.learning_objective: State the modern periodic law and explain why atomic number replaced atomic mass as its basis.
Describe the periods and groups of the long form of the Periodic Table and the number of elements in each period.

topics.title: Nomenclature of elements with atomic numbers greater than 100

concepts.learning_objective: Derive the IUPAC temporary name and symbol of an element from its atomic number.
Explain why IUPAC uses temporary names and how permanent names are given.

topics.title: Electronic configurations of elements and the Periodic Table

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the number of elements in a period to the orbitals filled in that period.
Recognise that elements of a group share the same valence shell configuration.

topics.title: s-, p-, d- and f-block elements; metals, non-metals and metalloids

concepts.learning_objective: Classify elements into s-, p-, d- and f-blocks from their outer electronic configurations and locate them in the table.
Distinguish metals, non-metals and metalloids and predict trends in metallic character.

topics.title: Periodic trends in atomic and ionic radii

concepts.learning_objective: Define covalent and metallic radius and explain the trends in atomic radius across a period and down a group.
Compare the sizes of ions with their parent atoms and of isoelectronic species.

topics.title: Ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy and electronegativity

concepts.learning_objective: Define ionization enthalpy and explain its periodic trends and exceptions.
Define electron gain enthalpy and explain its trends, including the exceptions of O and F.
Describe electronegativity, the Pauling scale and its periodic trends.

topics.title: Periodic trends in chemical properties and chemical reactivity

concepts.learning_objective: Predict valence, formulas of compounds and oxidation states from the position of elements.
Explain the anomalous behaviour of second period elements and the diagonal relationship.
Relate chemical reactivity across a period to the acidic, basic, amphoteric or neutral nature of oxides.
